absent: Numeric MSR identities, hypercall numbers, and feature bit positions.
GHCB layout and SEV-ES exit protocol beyond register transfer and success reporting.
CPUID base discovery, late guest initialization, and APIC IPI setup internals.
e820 table ownership and locking and full forced-MTRR semantics.
VDSO pvclock data layout and CPU0 pointer publication guarantees.
LDT descriptor layout, table loading, selector encoding, and deallocation path.
Scheduler clock stability criteria beyond the stable indication.
Host kick and poll-control protocol guarantees and failure modes.

findings.text: Early KVM clock setup selects newer versus legacy host time identities from advertised clock features, aborts when paravirt is unavailable or disabled or no clock feature exists, establishes per-CPU area handling, publishes the boot CPU area, derives scheduler offset and stability, wires platform calibration and wallclock and scheduler state hooks plus secondary CPU registration, presets the delay loop from the TSC rate, promotes clocksource rating under stable invariant TSC, then registers the clocksource and labels the provider.

Paravirt time reads use optimistic version validation around conversion of fresh TSC ticks with retry until stable; one mode optionally clears a guest-stopped indication and refreshes supervisory watchdogs; when global and sample stable indications are both set the converted value returns directly, otherwise a shared monotonic accumulator is consulted and updated by compare-exchange so concurrent or late readers never see time move backward.

TSC frequency estimate is derived from per-CPU scaling parameters by dividing a fixed scaled megahertz constant by the multiplier and then shifting according to a signed shift value, with calibration marking TSC frequency as known before returning the estimate and delay-loop preset derived from that rate.

Platform initialization under confidential guests with migration control installs a page encryption status notifier, reasserts encrypted status for every RAM extent and decrypted status for a dedicated BSS range through host calls, and arms migration readiness when not EFI booted; unconditionally it initializes the KVM clock, defers APIC setup to post-init, and forces a writeback default memory type with one uncached PCI hole sized from the top of low RAM.

The KVM hypervisor descriptor advertises name and type and binds detection, late guest initialization, x2APIC availability, extended MSI destination support, and platform initialization, plus SEV-ES hypercall preparation and completion hooks when memory encryption support is compiled in.

SEV-ES hypercall preparation transfers four guest integer argument registers into the shared call block while return register and privilege level are already present, and completion unconditionally reports success without return-state validation.
Boot finalization enables paravirt steal-time static branches when a steal clock was detected, including a runqueue accounting branch when steal accumulation is present.

Time paths avoid sleeping locks: per-CPU time pointers are accessed with preemption disabled in non-tracing regions, shared versioned fields use optimistic begin and retry checks with ordering barriers, monotonic enforcement uses atomic read and compare-exchange on a global accumulator, and LDT switching asserts non-preemptible context while reloading only when either address space owns a table.

Observed LDT state comprises a descriptor pointer sized to the requested entry count, a slot index initialized to unaliased, and an entry count; allocation rejects counts above the architectural maximum, zero-fills at least one page or a larger zeroed area, and on data failure releases the container and reports absence.

Observed clock state comprises a boot-resident wall page in decrypted storage, an optional overflow time-info array, per-CPU pointers to time-info blocks, read-only-after-init MSR identities and scheduler offset, and a clocksource descriptor with continuous 64-bit semantics, default mid-range rating, snapshot support tagging TSC hardware, and an enable hook recording paravirt VDSO use.

Per-CPU clock areas begin with CPU zero prepublished from a static boot array; later CPUs reuse an existing distinct pointer, otherwise consume successive static slots while available then successive overflow slots when allocated, failing when neither can satisfy the request; overflow setup is skipped when the static array covers all possible CPUs, otherwise it allocates, decrypts under confidential guests, and zeroes the area, while VDSO support is enabled only when paravirt is available and enabled and both boot pointer and stable indication allow it.

An address space moves from no LDT to owning a sized table exactly once, then through kernel and where applicable user page-table mapping with different sanity expectations for first versus later mappings, context-switch reloading whenever either predecessor or successor owns a table, owning-CPU-only flush reloading with cached segment refresh for LDT selectors, and cache reloading limited to data and extra segments on 64-bit builds.

Remote wakeup issues a host kick addressed by target APIC identity; paravirt waiting does nothing in nonmaskable context, otherwise halts or safely halts only while a one-byte condition still matches, disabling interrupts first when they were enabled; host halt polling is disabled when guest polling is enabled and re-enabled when guest polling is disabled through synchronous remote calls programming a poll-control state, with missing host support logged and treated as unavailable.

Wallclock retrieval programs the wall identity to the shared page address then combines it with current per-CPU time under disabled preemption, wallclock setting is uniformly unsupported, scheduler save is empty while restore re-registers the primary clock, secondary CPUs register on bringup, registration publishes the per-CPU block address with an enable bit and skips absent blocks, cycle reads use the non-watchdog path, snapshot reads also return raw ticks tagged to TSC hardware, and guest-paused polling clears the stopped flag and touches watchdogs when set.

Hazards include wall seconds limited to a 32-bit range covering only late twentieth to early twenty-second century dates, guest-stopped indications that must clear and refresh multiple watchdogs to avoid false hang reports, backward or concurrent samples requiring monotonic clamping, TSC instability preventing rating promotion, overflow allocation or decryption failures leaving later CPUs without clock areas, and LDT mapping mismatches under page-table isolation triggering warnings.
Boot time-info capacity is the number of vsyscall time-info records that fit in one page.
LDT slot stride is the product of maximum entry count and per-entry byte size, with a build-time expectation that entry size matches the architectural descriptor size.
